lane: G-103/G-104 tagged PDF render service (Revised Section 508, 504.2.2)
missionPremise: Generated PDFs across the SmartCity OS product line fail Revised Section 508 criterion 504.2.2. This is measured, not suspected: it is the single 'Does Not Support' row in a completed Accessibility Conformance Report going to the government distributor Vertosoft, which makes it the highest-value defect in the product line. Two paths fail for different reasons; this lane addresses path 1 (the hauska-engine site-plan export). Source: _dispatches/2026-08-20_pdf_dispatch.md, plus the operator ruling relayed mid-flight on 2026-08-20 that the site-plan generator is working software and all remediation must be ADDITIVE AND OPT-IN.
completionPredicate: A caller that opts in gets a site-plan PDF with /StructTreeRoot present, /MarkInfo /Marked true, /Lang set, a document title set, structure-tree order matching visual order on every sampled page, and materially reduced text fragmentation; the default export is byte-reachable and behaviourally identical to d3f3794; every acceptance check has been observed FAILING on a deliberate violation; and a CI-executed gate fails when any of that regresses. A stranger can evaluate this by running scripts/generate-site-plan-sample.mjs on d3f3794 and the tagged emitter on this branch and comparing with the instrument recorded below.
scopeBasis: The 2026-08-20 operator ruling excludes: modifying render.ts or dossier.ts, switching any existing caller, and touching smartcity-dashboards, smartcity-kit, smart-files, plan-review, or the ss/* programme's flood/containment/rail-scoring/statewide-audit code. It also removes the premise for the Playwright/Chromium shared render service, whose only named consumer was the site-plan path that is now explicitly not to be replaced. What is IN scope is therefore exactly: new files under packages/engine-core/src/site-plan/pdf/tagged/ in hauska-engine, plus a CI gate. smartcity-os was deliberately not opened.

instrumentDefectsFoundAndFixedDuringThis: `deref(mi.get('/Marked')) is True` is fail-CLOSED against pypdf: BooleanObject is never identical to Python True, so it reported all six conformant reference PDFs as unmarked. Found by disagreeing with the dispatch and checking who was wrong.

`bool(x)` is the obvious repair and is fail-OPEN: pypdf's BooleanObject defines no __bool__, so bool(BooleanObject(False)) is True and a PDF declaring /Marked false would have read as marked. Rejected before use. `== True` is correct in both directions and is what shipped.

not_done.item: Dispatch item 2, the shared Chromium/Playwright render service producing tagged PDFs from semantic markup, with the site-plan path wired to it
not_done.why: The 2026-08-20 operator ruling removed its premise. Its only named consumer was the site-plan path, and that path is now explicitly not to be replaced or repointed. Building the service anyway would add a heavyweight Playwright dependency to the monorepo with zero callers, which is a dormant mechanism by ENFORCEMENT's definition: it exists, it is correct, and it does nothing. The site-plan drawing sheet is vector geometry (parcel ring, setback offsets, contours, collision-solved labels, orthophoto overlay) and cannot be expressed as semantic HTML without rewriting the renderer, which is the thing the ruling forbids.

not_done.item: Dispatch item 3, repointing the legacy SmartCity jsPDF export at the shared service
not_done.why: Not attempted. It cannot be done additively. Repointing client/src/lib/pdf-utils.ts, reportPdf.ts, ai-report-pdf.ts or department-pdf.ts changes the default output of a shipped product, which the ruling forbids; and the service it would point at does not exist as a deployed surface, so it would also need a new server route, which is itself a default-behaviour change. smartcity-os was therefore not opened at all: no branch, no commit, no PR. The dispatch's characterisation of that path is unverified by me and should not be treated as confirmed by this close.

not_done.item: The literal 'under 2 percent single-character extracted lines' bar
not_done.why: Reached 2.61%. The four remaining lines are the north-arrow 'N' and the scale-bar '0' on two sheets each: genuine one-character labels. Closing the last 0.61 points requires changing what the sheet prints, which SITE PLAN SHEET STANDARD v1.2 governs and the additive ruling forbids. Reported rather than forced.

not_done.item: Heading structure and figure alternative text in the tagged output
not_done.why: A finished content stream carries no heading semantics and no image description. Inferring heading levels from font size would write a guess into a binding structure, and inventing alt text is worse than omitting it. Both require the renderer to declare them, which is an in-place change. Declared at runtime in TagPdfResult.declaredLimitations, not buried in a comment.

not_done.item: Tagging for the property dossier (dossier.ts) and the flood-drainage report (flood-drainage.ts)
not_done.why: Both are additional pdf-lib producers with the same defect class, and both were confirmed present in the tree. dossier.ts additionally appends site-plan sheets with pdf-lib copyPages, which carries marked content and DROPS the structure tree, so a naive fix there would leave copied pages marked with a dangling /StructParents: worse than untagged because the defect is invisible. Fixing it needs either an in-place change to dossier.ts or a second post-processor pass over the assembled document. Out of scope under the additive ruling; recorded as leave-behind.

contradictionsWithTheDispatch.dispatchSaid: path 1's more serious defect is glyph-by-glyph drawing, so tagging alone will not fix it
contradictionsWithTheDispatch.measured: correct as a diagnosis, but the remedy does not require changing the renderer. pdf-lib emits each glyph as its own BT..ET with a trailing T*, and it is the T* that makes an extractor break the line. Merging the blocks while preserving each glyph's ABSOLUTE Tm removes the line breaks with no coordinate recomputed: 458 of 458 glyph-show operations verified identical in position, size and glyph.
contradictionsWithTheDispatch.assessment: a correction in the useful direction: the fix was reachable inside the additive constraint, which was not obvious from the brief

contradictionsWithTheDispatch.measured: true of the drawText API, but PDFOperatorNames.SetCharacterSpacing ('Tc') exists and page.pushOperators reaches it, so an in-place fix was available. It was built, measured at 2.52 percent, and then REVERTED when the additive ruling arrived. Recorded here so the option is not rediscovered from scratch.
